subject: Biology
questionText: Which statement about taxonomic categories is correct?
options: Genus is a group of related species; a family is a group of related genera
A species can belong to more than one genus
Class comes between genus and family
explanation: Hierarchy: species < genus < family < order < class < phylum/division < kingdom.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which of these is a defining feature of all living organisms, with no exception?
explanation: Growth and reproduction are not defining (non-living things also grow by accumulation; mules and worker bees don't reproduce). Metabolism, cellular organisation and consciousness are defining features.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which feature is common to all members of the kingdom Monera?
options: Presence of a cell wall made of cellulose
explanation: Monera (bacteria) are prokaryotes; nutrition varies and the wall (when present) is made of peptidoglycan, not cellulose.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which statement about viroids is correct?
options: They are DNA viruses with a lipid envelope
They are free RNA without a protein coat and cause potato spindle tuber disease
explanation: T.O. Diener (1971) found viroids: small, free RNA, smaller than viruses.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which pair of organism and cell-wall feature is correctly matched?
options: Mycoplasma — no cell wall, smallest living cells
Euglena — has a cellulose cell wall
explanation: Mycoplasma lack a cell wall. Euglena has a protein-rich pellicle; diatom walls are siliceous; archaebacterial walls are not peptidoglycan.

subject: Biology
questionText: Sac fungi, whose sexual spores are formed endogenously in asci, belong to
explanation: Ascospores form inside asci (e.g. Penicillium, Neurospora, yeast).

subject: Biology
questionText: Lichens are a symbiotic association between
options: fungi and roots of higher plants
explanation: The algal partner (phycobiont) makes food; the fungal partner (mycobiont) gives shelter and absorbs water. Mycorrhiza is fungus + root.

subject: Biology
questionText: In bryophytes, the main plant body is
explanation: In mosses and liverworts the dominant plant is the gametophyte; the sporophyte is attached to and depends on it.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which pair of algae and stored food is correctly matched?
explanation: Green: starch; brown: laminarin/mannitol; red: floridean starch.

subject: Biology
questionText: In gymnosperms, the ovules are
options: naked, not enclosed in an ovary
explanation: Gymno = naked; there is no ovary wall, so no fruit is formed.

subject: Biology
questionText: Heterospory (two kinds of spores) is seen in
explanation: Selaginella and Salvinia produce microspores and megaspores — a step towards the seed habit.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which group shows a pseudocoelom?
explanation: The body cavity is not lined by mesoderm; flatworms are acoelomate, annelids and arthropods are coelomate.

subject: Biology
questionText: Metameric segmentation is first seen in
explanation: Earthworms show true metamerism.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which feature is shared by all chordates at some stage of life?
options: Notochord, dorsal hollow nerve cord and pharyngeal gill slits
explanation: These three, plus a post-anal tail, define chordates; the vertebral column is only in vertebrates.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which pair of animal and excretory structure is correct?
explanation: Flame cells: flatworms; nephridia: annelids; Malpighian tubules: insects; green glands: prawn.

subject: Biology
questionText: Water vascular system and radial symmetry in adults are characteristic of
explanation: Echinoderm adults are radially symmetrical; larvae are bilateral.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which statement about mammals is correct?
options: They have mammary glands, external ears (pinna) and hair on the skin
explanation: Platypus lays eggs (oviparous); mammals have a four-chambered heart and are homoiothermous.

subject: Biology
questionText: In the family Fabaceae, the flower shows
options: twisted aestivation and an inferior ovary
valvate aestivation and an epiphyllous androecium
vexillary aestivation and a monocarpellary superior ovary
a bicarpellary syncarpous ovary with axile placentation
explanation: Fabaceae (pea family): papilionaceous corolla with vexillary aestivation, diadelphous stamens, monocarpellary ovary with marginal placentation.

subject: Biology
questionText: The edible part of the coconut is
explanation: Coconut is a drupe; its white kernel and the 'water' are endosperm.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which example of placentation is correct?
options: Marginal — pea; axile — tomato; free central — Dianthus
explanation: Parietal: mustard, Argemone; basal: sunflower, marigold.

subject: Biology
questionText: Pneumatophores, which help in respiration, are found in
explanation: Roots grow up out of the swampy soil to get oxygen.

subject: Biology
questionText: A transverse section shows scattered vascular bundles with bundle sheath, no secondary growth, and no distinct ground tissue zones. It is
explanation: Scattered, closed bundles surrounded by sclerenchymatous sheath are typical of monocot stems (e.g. maize).

subject: Biology
questionText: Casparian strips are found in the
explanation: Suberin bands on the radial and tangential walls of endodermal cells block apoplastic water flow.

subject: Biology
questionText: In the dorsiventral (dicot) leaf, the palisade parenchyma lies
explanation: Isobilateral (monocot) leaves lack this differentiation.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which tissue is matched with its location correctly?
options: Squamous epithelium — lining of the stomach
Cuboidal epithelium — walls of blood vessels
Ciliated epithelium — inner lining of bronchioles and fallopian tubes
Columnar epithelium — air sacs of lungs
explanation: Squamous: blood vessel walls and alveoli; cuboidal: ducts of glands, PCT; columnar: stomach and intestine lining.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which junction helps to stop substances from leaking across a tissue?
explanation: Gap junctions connect cytoplasm of cells; adhering junctions hold cells together.

subject: Biology
questionText: Tendons and ligaments are examples of
explanation: Collagen fibres in parallel bundles; tendons join muscle to bone, ligaments bone to bone.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which organelle is NOT bounded by a membrane?
explanation: Ribosomes, centrioles and the cytoskeleton lack membranes.

subject: Biology
questionText: The 70S ribosome of prokaryotes is made of
explanation: 80S (eukaryotes) = 60S + 40S; S units are not additive.

subject: Biology
questionText: Centrioles and basal bodies have a microtubule arrangement of
explanation: Cilia and flagella axonemes are 9 + 2.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which organelle is the site of synthesis of lipids and steroid hormones?
explanation: SER makes lipids; RER (with ribosomes) makes proteins.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which statement about enzymes and enzyme inhibition is correct?
options: All enzymes are made of RNA
Competitive inhibitors resemble the substrate and bind to the active site
A non-competitive inhibitor must resemble the substrate
explanation: Malonate inhibits succinic dehydrogenase competitively. Enzymes lower activation energy; most are proteins (ribozymes are RNA).

subject: Biology
questionText: Which of these is NOT a polymer?
explanation: Lecithin is a phospholipid; lipids are not strictly macromolecular polymers. The others are polymers.

subject: Biology
questionText: The most abundant protein in animals and the most abundant protein in the biosphere are, respectively,
explanation: NCERT: collagen in animal world; RuBisCO in the whole biosphere.

subject: Biology
questionText: Crossing over occurs during which stage of meiosis?
explanation: Recombination nodules appear and crossing over occurs at pachytene; chiasmata become visible at diplotene.

subject: Biology
questionText: A cell has 20 pg of DNA in G₁. The DNA content after S phase and in each daughter cell after mitosis are
explanation: DNA doubles in S phase (2C → 4C) and is halved between the two daughter cells.

subject: Biology
questionText: During which phase does the cell's chromosome number stay the same while DNA content doubles?
explanation: Replication makes sister chromatids; chromosome number does not change.

subject: Biology
questionText: The terminalisation of chiasmata takes place in
explanation: Diakinesis is the last stage of prophase I.

subject: Biology
questionText: In the C₄ pathway, the first stable product of CO₂ fixation and the primary acceptor are, respectively,
explanation: PEP carboxylase in mesophyll cells fixes CO₂ into OAA (4-C).

subject: Biology
questionText: Kranz anatomy is characteristic of
options: C₄ plants such as maize and sugarcane
explanation: Large bundle-sheath cells around the veins carry out the Calvin cycle.

subject: Biology
questionText: To make one molecule of glucose, the Calvin cycle requires
explanation: Six turns of the cycle: each turn uses 3 ATP and 2 NADPH.

subject: Biology
questionText: In cyclic photophosphorylation,
options: only PS I is involved and only ATP is formed
both PS I and PS II work and NADPH is formed
explanation: Electrons return to PS I; no NADPH and no O₂ are produced.

subject: Biology
questionText: Photorespiration does NOT occur in C₄ plants mainly because
options: CO₂ concentration around RuBisCO in bundle-sheath cells is kept high
explanation: High CO₂ makes RuBisCO act as a carboxylase, not an oxygenase.

subject: Biology
questionText: The net gain of ATP from one glucose in glycolysis is
explanation: 4 ATP are made, 2 are used; 2 NADH are also produced.

subject: Biology
questionText: The respiratory quotient (RQ) of tripalmitin (a fat) is about
explanation: 2C₅₁H₉₈O₆ + 145O₂ → 102CO₂ + 98H₂O; RQ = 102/145 ≈ 0.7. Carbohydrates: 1.0; anaerobic: infinite.

subject: Biology
questionText: In the Krebs cycle, substrate-level phosphorylation (forming GTP) occurs when
options: citric acid is converted to α-ketoglutaric acid
malic acid is converted to oxaloacetic acid
succinyl-CoA is converted to succinic acid
explanation: NCERT: the conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinic acid is accompanied by synthesis of one GTP.

subject: Biology
questionText: In the electron transport chain, the final electron acceptor is
explanation: Cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV) passes electrons to O₂, forming water.

subject: Biology
questionText: The 'foolish seedling' (bakanae) disease of rice led to the discovery of
explanation: E. Kurosawa found the fungus Gibberella fujikuroi secretes the substance responsible.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which plant growth regulator is a gas and promotes fruit ripening?
explanation: Ethylene also promotes senescence and abscission.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which hormone is called the stress hormone and causes stomatal closure?
explanation: ABA increases tolerance to stress and induces seed dormancy.

subject: Biology
questionText: Apical dominance is caused by
explanation: Removing the tip (decapitation) lets lateral buds grow, as in tea plantations and hedges.

subject: Biology
questionText: About what percentage of CO₂ is carried by blood as bicarbonate?
explanation: ≈70% as bicarbonate, 20–25% as carbamino-haemoglobin, ≈7% dissolved in plasma.

subject: Biology
questionText: Vital capacity equals
explanation: Adding RV gives total lung capacity.

subject: Biology
questionText: The oxygen dissociation curve shifts to the right when
options: pCO₂ rises, H⁺ rises and temperature rises
explanation: Conditions in tissues favour O₂ release (Bohr effect).

subject: Biology
questionText: In a normal ECG, the QRS complex represents
explanation: P wave: atrial depolarisation; T wave: ventricular repolarisation.

subject: Biology
questionText: The pacemaker of the human heart is the
explanation: The SAN generates about 70–75 action potentials per minute.

subject: Biology
questionText: Erythroblastosis foetalis can occur when
options: an Rh-positive mother carries an Rh-negative foetus
an Rh-negative mother carries an Rh-positive foetus (usually in a second pregnancy)
the mother has blood group O
explanation: Anti-Rh antibodies made after the first delivery can cross the placenta and destroy foetal RBCs.

subject: Biology
questionText: The duration of one cardiac cycle at 72 beats per minute is about

subject: Biology
questionText: Which part of the nephron is impermeable to water?
options: Collecting duct in the presence of ADH
explanation: The ascending limb pumps out salts but not water, helping set up the medullary gradient.

subject: Biology
questionText: The counter-current mechanism in the kidney is maintained by
explanation: It keeps an increasing osmolarity (300 to 1200 mOsm/L) towards the inner medulla.

subject: Biology
questionText: The glomerular filtration rate in a healthy adult is about
explanation: Of about 180 L filtered each day, about 1.5 L leaves as urine.

subject: Biology
questionText: Ammonotelic, ureotelic and uricotelic animals are, respectively, examples of
explanation: Aquatic animals excrete ammonia; mammals urea; birds, reptiles and insects uric acid.

subject: Biology
questionText: During muscle contraction, which band shortens?
options: The A band together with the I band
explanation: Thin filaments slide over thick ones; the A band (length of thick filaments) stays the same.

subject: Biology
questionText: Calcium ions start muscle contraction by binding to
options: troponin, which moves tropomyosin off the actin binding sites
explanation: This uncovers active sites on actin for myosin cross-bridges.

subject: Biology
questionText: The joint between atlas and axis vertebrae is a
explanation: Saddle joint: carpal and metacarpal of the thumb; hinge: knee; ball and socket: shoulder.

subject: Biology
questionText: During the resting state of a neuron,
options: the outside of the axon membrane is positive relative to the inside
the membrane is freely permeable to Na⁺
explanation: The Na⁺/K⁺ pump (3 Na⁺ out, 2 K⁺ in) and leaky K⁺ channels give a resting potential of about −70 mV inside.

subject: Biology
questionText: Nerve impulses pass fastest in
options: myelinated fibres, by saltatory conduction between nodes of Ranvier
explanation: The impulse jumps from node to node.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which hormone pair is antagonistic in regulating blood glucose?
explanation: Insulin lowers glucose (hypoglycaemic); glucagon raises it (hyperglycaemic).

subject: Biology
questionText: Parathyroid hormone
explanation: PTH is hypercalcaemic; thyrocalcitonin lowers calcium.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which hormone acts through an intracellular (nuclear) receptor?
explanation: Steroid and iodothyronine hormones enter cells; protein hormones act through membrane receptors and second messengers.

subject: Biology
questionText: In a typical angiosperm embryo sac, the number of cells and nuclei are
explanation: Egg apparatus (3) + antipodals (3) + central cell with 2 polar nuclei.

subject: Biology
questionText: The ploidy of the nucellus, endosperm and embryo in angiosperms is, respectively,
explanation: Nucellus is maternal tissue (2n); endosperm from triple fusion (3n); embryo from zygote (2n).

subject: Biology
questionText: Geitonogamy is
options: transfer of pollen within the same flower
transfer of pollen to the stigma of another flower on the same plant
transfer of pollen to a flower of a different plant
explanation: It is functionally cross-pollination but genetically like self-pollination.

subject: Biology
questionText: A fruit that develops without fertilisation is called
explanation: Banana is an example; it can be induced by growth hormones.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which cells of the testis secrete androgens?
explanation: Sertoli cells nourish developing sperm.

subject: Biology
questionText: Ovulation in a 28-day menstrual cycle occurs around the 14th day due to
explanation: High oestrogen triggers the mid-cycle LH (and FSH) surge that ruptures the Graafian follicle.

subject: Biology
questionText: Implantation of the human blastocyst normally occurs in the
explanation: Fertilisation occurs at the ampullary–isthmic junction; the blastocyst implants in the uterine wall.

subject: Biology
questionText: One primary oocyte forms how many functional ova at the end of oogenesis?
explanation: The divisions are unequal; polar bodies degenerate.

subject: Biology
questionText: Copper-releasing IUDs prevent conception mainly by
options: suppressing sperm motility and fertilising capacity
changing the pH of the vagina to alkaline
explanation: Cu-T and Multiload 375 release Cu ions.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which method allows the embryo to be transferred into the fallopian tube when it has up to 8 blastomeres?
explanation: ZIFT: zygote/early embryo (up to 8 cells) into the fallopian tube; IUT: embryo with more than 8 cells into the uterus.

subject: Biology
questionText: In a dihybrid cross, the F₂ phenotypic ratio 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 shows
options: independent assortment of the two genes
explanation: Two genes on different chromosomes assort independently.

subject: Biology
questionText: A test cross of a plant with the dominant phenotype gives 1 : 1 offspring. The plant was
explanation: Crossing with the homozygous recessive gives all dominant if the plant is homozygous, 1 : 1 if heterozygous.

subject: Biology
questionText: A man of blood group A and a woman of blood group B have a child of blood group O. The genotypes of the parents are
explanation: An O child (I°I°) needs one I° from each parent.

subject: Biology
questionText: In snapdragon, a cross between red (RR) and white (rr) flowered plants gives pink F₁. The F₂ phenotypic ratio is
explanation: Incomplete dominance: genotypic and phenotypic ratios are the same.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which disorder is caused by trisomy of chromosome 21?
explanation: Turner's: 45, X0; Klinefelter's: 47, XXY; PKU is an autosomal recessive Mendelian disorder.

subject: Biology
questionText: Sex of the offspring in birds is decided by
explanation: In birds the male is ZZ and the female ZW.

subject: Biology
questionText: If a double-stranded DNA has 20% cytosine, the percentage of adenine is
explanation: C = G = 20% → A + T = 60% → A = 30% (Chargaff's rule).

subject: Biology
questionText: In E. coli, the lac operon is switched ON when
options: lactose (allolactose) binds the repressor and inactivates it
the i gene is deleted only
explanation: The inducer prevents the repressor from binding the operator, so RNA polymerase transcribes z, y and a genes.

subject: Biology
questionText: During DNA replication, the lagging strand is synthesised
options: discontinuously as Okazaki fragments joined by DNA ligase
explanation: DNA polymerase works only 5′→3′, so one strand is made in pieces.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which statement about the genetic code is correct?
options: Each amino acid has exactly one codon
It is degenerate, unambiguous and nearly universal
explanation: AUG codes methionine (and is the start codon); UAA, UAG, UGA are stop codons.

subject: Biology
questionText: In eukaryotes, the removal of introns and joining of exons is called
explanation: Capping adds methyl-guanosine at the 5′ end; tailing adds poly-A at the 3′ end.

subject: Biology
questionText: VNTRs used in DNA fingerprinting belong to
explanation: Variable number tandem repeats differ greatly between individuals.

subject: Biology
questionText: The wings of a butterfly and of a bird are
explanation: Same function, different origin.

subject: Biology
questionText: Industrial melanism in peppered moths in England is an example of
explanation: Dark moths survived better on soot-covered trees, so their frequency rose.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which factor does NOT disturb Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium?
explanation: Gene migration, drift, mutation, recombination and selection change allele frequencies.

subject: Biology
questionText: If the frequency of the recessive allele in a population in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium is 0.3, the frequency of heterozygotes is

subject: Biology
questionText: The infective stage of Plasmodium that enters the human body through the bite of a female Anopheles is the
explanation: Sporozoites go to the liver, then RBCs; gametocytes are picked up by the mosquito.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which disease is caused by a bacterium?
explanation: Typhoid: Salmonella typhi; malaria: Plasmodium (protozoan); common cold: rhinovirus; ringworm: fungi.

subject: Biology
questionText: HIV mainly attacks
explanation: Fall in helper T-cells weakens immunity, leading to opportunistic infections (AIDS).

subject: Biology
questionText: Antibodies are produced by
explanation: B-cells make antibodies (humoral immunity); T-cells give cell-mediated immunity.

subject: Biology
questionText: Colostrum gives the newborn passive immunity mainly through the antibody
explanation: Colostrum is rich in IgA.

subject: Biology
questionText: The bacterium that converts milk into curd is
explanation: LAB also increase vitamin B₁₂ in curd.

subject: Biology
questionText: Statins, used to lower blood cholesterol, are obtained from the yeast
explanation: Statins inhibit an enzyme of cholesterol synthesis; Trichoderma gives cyclosporin A.

subject: Biology
questionText: In a sewage treatment plant, flocs are
options: masses of bacteria associated with fungal filaments
explanation: Flocs digest organic matter and reduce the BOD during secondary treatment.

subject: Biology
questionText: EcoRI cuts DNA between
options: G and A in the sequence 5′-GAATTC-3′
explanation: It leaves sticky ends.

subject: Biology
questionText: In pBR322, insertional inactivation of the tetracycline resistance gene means recombinant colonies will
options: grow on ampicillin but not on tetracycline
grow on tetracycline but not on ampicillin
explanation: The foreign DNA in tetʳ destroys tetracycline resistance; ampʳ still works.

subject: Biology
questionText: In gel electrophoresis, DNA fragments move towards the
explanation: DNA is negatively charged; agarose acts as a sieve.

subject: Biology
questionText: The thermostable DNA polymerase used in PCR is obtained from
explanation: Taq polymerase works at high temperatures used in PCR cycles.

subject: Biology
questionText: The cry genes used to make Bt cotton come from
explanation: Bt toxin protein is activated in the alkaline gut of insects and kills them.

subject: Biology
questionText: RNA interference was used to protect tobacco plants against
explanation: dsRNA silences a specific mRNA of the nematode.

subject: Biology
questionText: Genetically engineered human insulin (Humulin) is made by producing
options: pro-insulin with the C-peptide in yeast only
A and B chains separately and joining them with disulphide bonds
explanation: Eli Lilly (1983) made the two chains in E. coli and linked them.

subject: Biology
questionText: The first clinical gene therapy (1990) was given to a 4-year-old girl with deficiency of
explanation: Lymphocytes with a functional ADA gene were returned to the patient.

subject: Biology
questionText: The logistic growth equation dN/dt = rN[(K − N)/K] describes
options: growth that slows down as the population approaches the carrying capacity
explanation: Verhulst–Pearl logistic growth gives a sigmoid curve.

subject: Biology
questionText: An interaction in which one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited is
explanation: Example: orchid growing on a mango branch; barnacles on a whale.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which population interaction is correctly paired?
options: Cattle egret and grazing cattle — parasitism
explanation: Cuscuta is a parasite; cattle egret–cattle and orchid–mango are commensalism.

subject: Biology
questionText: The 10% law of energy transfer between trophic levels was given by
explanation: Only about 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which ecological pyramid is always upright?
options: Pyramid of biomass in the sea
explanation: Energy is lost at each level, so it can never be inverted.

subject: Biology
questionText: Net primary productivity equals
options: gross primary productivity minus respiration losses
explanation: NPP = GPP − R; it is the biomass available to consumers.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which pair is an example of ex situ conservation?
explanation: Ex situ = off-site; in situ protects species in their natural habitat.

subject: Biology
questionText: According to Alexander von Humboldt, on a log–log scale species richness and area show
explanation: log S = log C + Z log A; Z is usually 0.1–0.2.

subject: Biology
questionText: The 'evil quartet' of causes of biodiversity loss includes habitat loss, over-exploitation, alien species invasion and
explanation: When a host goes extinct, its unique parasites go with it.

subject: Biology
questionText: The 'transforming principle' was discovered (1928) using Streptococcus pneumoniae and mice by
explanation: Heat-killed S strain transformed live R strain into virulent bacteria.

subject: Biology
questionText: The biochemical nature of the transforming principle was shown to be DNA by
explanation: Protein- and RNA-digesting enzymes did not stop transformation; DNase did.

subject: Biology
questionText: Unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material came from bacteriophage experiments with radioactive ³²P and ³⁵S by
explanation: Hershey and Chase (1952): only ³²P-labelled DNA entered the bacteria.

subject: Biology
questionText: Semi-conservative replication of DNA was proved in E. coli using ¹⁵N by
explanation: Meselson and Stahl (1958) used CsCl density gradient centrifugation.

subject: Biology
questionText: Semi-conservative replication of chromosomes was shown in Vicia faba using radioactive thymidine by
explanation: Taylor (1958) in faba beans.

subject: Biology
questionText: The double-helix model of DNA (1953) was proposed by Watson and Crick using the X-ray diffraction data of
explanation: Chargaff's base ratios were also used.

subject: Biology
questionText: DNA was first identified (as 'nuclein') in 1869 by
explanation: Meischer isolated an acidic substance from the nucleus.

subject: Biology
questionText: The lac operon model of gene regulation was given by
explanation: Francois Jacob and Jacques Monod first described a transcriptionally regulated system.

subject: Biology
questionText: The suggestion that the genetic code must be a triplet came from the physicist
explanation: Gamow argued 4 bases must code 20 amino acids, so codons need at least 3 bases.

subject: Biology
questionText: The chemical method to synthesise RNA molecules with defined combinations of bases, which helped decipher the code, was developed by
explanation: Nirenberg's cell-free system and Ochoa's enzyme (polynucleotide phosphorylase) also helped.

subject: Biology
questionText: The technique of DNA fingerprinting was initially developed by
explanation: Jeffreys used VNTR probes.

subject: Biology
questionText: Mendel's work was independently rediscovered in 1900 by
options: de Vries, Correns and von Tschermak
explanation: Their rediscovery started modern genetics.

subject: Biology
questionText: The chromosomal theory of inheritance was proposed by
explanation: They linked chromosome movement in meiosis to Mendel's factors.

subject: Biology
questionText: Linkage and recombination were demonstrated experimentally using Drosophila by
explanation: Morgan coined the term linkage.

subject: Biology
questionText: Recombination frequency was first used to map the positions of genes on a chromosome by
explanation: Sturtevant, Morgan's student.

subject: Biology
questionText: A structure called the 'X body' was first seen in insect spermatogenesis (1891) by
explanation: It was later named the X chromosome.

subject: Biology
questionText: The mutation theory of evolution, based on work with evening primrose (Oenothera), was given by
explanation: He called large sudden variations 'saltation'.

subject: Biology
questionText: Who reached conclusions on natural selection similar to Darwin's while working in the Malay Archipelago?
explanation: Wallace and Darwin presented their ideas together.

subject: Biology
questionText: The idea that evolution occurs by use and disuse of organs (e.g. the giraffe's neck) was given by
explanation: Inheritance of acquired characters is now not accepted.

subject: Biology
questionText: The experiment showing that amino acids can form from CH₄, H₂, NH₃ and water vapour under electric discharge (1953) was done by
explanation: It supported the chemical origin of life proposed by Oparin and Haldane.

subject: Biology
questionText: The view that life comes only from pre-existing life was demonstrated with sterilised flasks by
explanation: Life did not arise in pre-sterilised flasks with killed yeast.

subject: Biology
questionText: The statement 'Omnis cellula-e cellula' (new cells arise from pre-existing cells) was given by
explanation: Virchow (1855) modified the cell theory of Schleiden and Schwann.

subject: Biology
questionText: The nucleus was first described (1831) by
explanation: Brown observed it in orchid cells.

subject: Biology
questionText: The Golgi apparatus was first observed (1898) by
explanation: He saw densely stained reticular structures near the nucleus.

subject: Biology
questionText: Ribosomes were first observed under the electron microscope as dense particles (1953) by
explanation: Ribosomes are made of RNA and proteins.

subject: Biology
questionText: The five-kingdom classification was proposed (1969) by
explanation: Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia.

subject: Biology
questionText: The term 'contagium vivum fluidum' (infectious living fluid) for viruses was given by
explanation: Beijerinck (1898) found extracts of infected tobacco remained infectious after filtering.

subject: Biology
questionText: Viruses were shown to be crystallisable and mostly made of proteins (1935) by
explanation: Crystals of tobacco mosaic virus.

subject: Biology
questionText: The biologist called 'the Darwin of the 20th century', who proposed the biological species concept, is
explanation: NCERT mentions Mayr in The Living World.

subject: Biology
questionText: Auxin was first isolated from the coleoptile tips of oat seedlings by
explanation: Earlier, Charles and Francis Darwin had observed phototropism in canary grass coleoptiles.

subject: Biology
questionText: Kinetin, the first cytokinin, was identified from autoclaved herring sperm DNA by
explanation: They also showed the auxin–cytokinin ratio controls shoot and root formation in culture.

subject: Biology
questionText: The ripening effect of gases from ripened oranges on bananas (ethylene) was first noted by
explanation: Cousins (1910).

subject: Biology
questionText: Using a bell jar with a candle and a mouse, the role of plants in restoring air was shown (1770) by
explanation: Priestley's 'mint plant' experiment.

subject: Biology
questionText: That sunlight is essential for plants to purify air was shown by
explanation: He used an aquatic plant in bright light and darkness.

subject: Biology
questionText: The first action spectrum of photosynthesis was described using Cladophora and aerobic bacteria by
explanation: Bacteria gathered mainly in blue and red light regions.

subject: Biology
questionText: Using purple and green bacteria, it was shown that the O₂ evolved by green plants comes from water, not CO₂, by
explanation: Generalised equation: 2H₂A + CO₂ → 2A + CH₂O + H₂O.

subject: Biology
questionText: The path of carbon in the dark reactions was traced using radioactive ¹⁴C by
explanation: Hence the Calvin cycle (C₃ cycle).

subject: Biology
questionText: Who is known as the Father of Ecology in India?
explanation: NCERT notes his contribution to ecology research in India.

subject: Biology
questionText: The principle that two closely related species competing for the same resources cannot coexist indefinitely was given by
explanation: Gause's competitive exclusion principle.

subject: Biology
questionText: The 'rivet popper hypothesis' to explain the importance of species in an ecosystem was given by
explanation: Losing species is like losing rivets from an aeroplane wing.

subject: Biology
questionText: Long-term experiments showing that plots with more species have less year-to-year variation in biomass were done by
explanation: Increased diversity contributes to higher productivity and stability.

subject: Biology
questionText: Penicillin was discovered by Alexander Fleming; its full potential as an antibiotic was established by
explanation: Fleming, Chain and Florey shared the 1945 Nobel Prize.

subject: Biology
questionText: The first recombinant DNA was constructed (1972) by linking an antibiotic resistance gene to a plasmid of Salmonella typhimurium by
explanation: This marked the birth of genetic engineering.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which is an example of a stem modified into a tendril?
explanation: Stem tendrils in cucurbits and grapevine; leaf tendrils in pea.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which plant has a phylloclade (flattened green stem)?
explanation: Bougainvillea and Citrus have thorns; potato has a tuber.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which plant has an underground stem that stores food as a tuber?
explanation: Sweet potato, carrot and turnip are modified roots.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which of these is a C₄ plant?
explanation: Maize, sugarcane and sorghum are common C₄ plants.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which is an example of water pollination (hydrophily)?
explanation: Vallisneria and Hydrilla are water-pollinated; maize is wind-pollinated.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which plant shows apomixis (seeds without fertilisation)?
options: Some grasses and members of Asteraceae
explanation: NCERT: apomixis occurs in a few species of Asteraceae and grasses.

subject: Biology
questionText: Bioluminescence is well marked in
explanation: NCERT: bioluminescence (emission of light) is well marked in ctenophores such as Pleurobrachia.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which of these is a jawless vertebrate (cyclostome)?
explanation: Cyclostomes have a sucking, circular mouth without jaws.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which pair is an example of homologous organs?
options: Forelimbs of whale, bat and cheetah
explanation: Same basic structure, different functions — divergent evolution.

subject: Biology
questionText: Australian marsupials evolving from a common ancestor into many forms is an example of
explanation: Darwin's finches are another example.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which is an example of brood parasitism?
options: Cuckoo laying eggs in a crow's nest
explanation: The host bird raises the parasite's young.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which microbe is used commercially to produce citric acid?
explanation: Acetobacter → acetic acid; Clostridium → butyric acid; Lactobacillus → lactic acid.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which organism is used as a biofertiliser in paddy fields?
options: Cyanobacteria such as Anabaena and Nostoc
explanation: They fix atmospheric nitrogen.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which bacterium produces biogas (methane) from cellulosic material?
explanation: Methanogens live in anaerobic sludge and in the rumen of cattle.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which disease is caused by a helminth?
explanation: Ascaris (roundworm) causes ascariasis.

subject: Biology
questionText: The vector of dengue and chikungunya is
explanation: Culex transmits filariasis; Anopheles transmits malaria.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which transgenic animals are being developed to test the safety of vaccines before use on humans?
explanation: NCERT: transgenic mice are used for vaccine safety testing (e.g. polio vaccine).

subject: Biology
questionText: Which is an example of a recent extinction mentioned by NCERT?
explanation: Dodo (Mauritius), quagga (Africa), thylacine (Australia) and Steller's sea cow (Russia) are listed.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which is an example of an alien species that caused decline of native species?
explanation: Nile perch led to the extinction of over 200 cichlid fish species.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which alga is used to make agar?
explanation: Agar from red algae is used in culture media.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which of these is a liverwort?
explanation: Funaria and Sphagnum are mosses; Equisetum is a pteridophyte.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which is a surgical method of contraception in males?
explanation: Part of the vas deferens is cut and tied.

subject: Biology
questionText: The smallest cells, with no cell wall, are ____ (about 0.3 μm).
explanation: NCERT: Mycoplasma are the smallest living cells.

subject: Biology
questionText: The 'suicidal bags' of the cell are ____.
explanation: They contain hydrolytic enzymes active at acidic pH.

subject: Biology
questionText: The bond joining two amino acids in a protein is a ____ bond.
explanation: Formed by dehydration between –COOH and –NH₂.

subject: Biology
questionText: The stage of mitosis in which chromosomes line up at the equator is ____.
explanation: Spindle fibres attach to kinetochores.

subject: Biology
questionText: The enzyme that fixes CO₂ in the Calvin cycle is ____.
explanation: RuBisCO is the most abundant enzyme on Earth.

subject: Biology
questionText: The Krebs cycle takes place in the ____ of the mitochondrion.
explanation: Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm; the Krebs cycle and link reaction in the matrix.

subject: Biology
questionText: The volume of air that remains in the lungs even after forcible expiration is the ____ volume.
explanation: RV is about 1100–1200 mL.

subject: Biology
questionText: The blood group called the universal donor is ____.
explanation: Group O has no A or B antigens on the RBC surface.

subject: Biology
questionText: The functional unit of the kidney is the ____.
explanation: Each kidney has about one million nephrons.

subject: Biology
questionText: The functional contractile unit of a skeletal muscle fibre is the ____.
explanation: The part between two Z lines.

subject: Biology
questionText: The gap between two neurons where impulses pass is called a ____.
explanation: It can be electrical or chemical.

subject: Biology
questionText: Diabetes insipidus is caused by deficiency of the hormone ____.
explanation: Without ADH, large amounts of dilute urine are lost.

subject: Biology
questionText: The hormone detected in pregnancy tests is ____.
explanation: Secreted by the placenta.

subject: Biology
questionText: Amniocentesis tests for genetic disorders by examining cells in the ____ fluid.
explanation: Its misuse for sex determination is banned in India.

subject: Biology
questionText: The number of chromosomes in a person with Turner's syndrome is ____.
explanation: Karyotype 45, X0.

subject: Biology
questionText: The enzyme that joins Okazaki fragments is DNA ____.
explanation: It seals the nicks between fragments.

subject: Biology
questionText: Life is believed to have appeared on Earth about ____ billion years ago.
explanation: NCERT: life appeared about 500 million years after Earth formed, about 4 billion years ago.

subject: Biology
questionText: The causal organism of amoebiasis is Entamoeba ____.
explanation: Spread by houseflies contaminating food and water.

subject: Biology
questionText: The yeast used in making bread and brewing is Saccharomyces ____.
explanation: It ferments sugars to CO₂ and ethanol.

subject: Biology
questionText: Restriction enzymes recognise specific base sequences called ____ sequences that read the same on both strands.
explanation: E.g. 5′-GAATTC-3′ / 3′-CTTAAG-5′.

subject: Biology
questionText: The first transgenic cow, whose milk contained human alpha-lactalbumin, was named ____.
explanation: Produced in 1997.

subject: Biology
questionText: The maximum population size that an environment can support is called its ____ capacity.
explanation: Symbol K in the logistic equation.

subject: Biology
questionText: The rate of biomass production per unit area over a time period is called ____.
explanation: Expressed as g m⁻² yr⁻¹ or kcal m⁻² yr⁻¹.

subject: Biology
questionText: Regions with very high species richness and endemism under threat are called biodiversity ____.
explanation: Three hotspots — Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Indo-Burma and Himalaya — cover India's richest regions (NCERT).

subject: Biology
questionText: The scientific name Mangifera indica is written according to
explanation: Genus name first (capital), species epithet second (small), printed in italics.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which tissue in plants conducts food?
explanation: Phloem has sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and fibres.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which muscle is involuntary and striated?
explanation: Cardiac muscle has striations but works without conscious control.

subject: Biology
questionText: Which blood cells are the most numerous?
explanation: About 5–5.5 million per mm³.

subject: Biology
questionText: Spermatogenesis starts at puberty due to an increase in the secretion of
explanation: GnRH stimulates LH and FSH from the anterior pituitary.

subject: Biology
questionText: Gout is caused by
options: accumulation of uric acid crystals in joints
explanation: Osteoporosis: reduced bone mass; myasthenia gravis: autoimmune disorder.

subject: Biology
questionText: The part of the brain that controls respiration and cardiovascular reflexes is the
explanation: Medulla contains centres for breathing, heart rate and gastric secretions.

subject: Biology
questionText: The hormone melatonin is secreted by the
explanation: It regulates the 24-hour rhythm of the body.
